themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints in CD 411 surged to 6 THIS WEEK—an 1100% spike versus the 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—signaling a potential pest crisis requiring immediate investigation into whether structural or sanitation conditions are enabling spread.
evidence: 6 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.0, severity: high)
1100% spike represents statistically extreme deviation from baseline
Timing aligns with winter months when rodent populations typically seek shelter indoors
reporting_angles: Interview residents in affected blocks about rodent sightings, entry points, and health concerns
Investigate whether sanitation service cutbacks or delayed street cleaning in Bayside/Douglaston neighborhoods are contributing to food sources

themes_detail.label: Mold Reports Explode
themes_detail.summary: Mold complaints jumped to 4 LAST WEEK—a 3100% spike from the 0.1 weekly baseline over 8 weeks—potentially reflecting water damage from recent weather or unaddressed building moisture issues affecting residential units.
evidence: 4 mold complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72, severity: high)
3100% spike is the largest proportional increase in the dataset
Mold complaints clustered in residential complaints; correlates with winter moisture and heating season
reporting_angles: Survey residents about water leaks, basement flooding, or HVAC issues in recent weeks
Cross-reference with Heat/Hot Water complaints (336 total over 90 days) to identify buildings with systemic moisture/heating failures

themes_detail.label: Traffic Congestion Spike
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints in CD 411 hit 5 THIS WEEK—a 700% jump versus the 0.6 weekly average—suggesting new congestion patterns, possibly tied to construction activity or changes in commuter behavior.
evidence: 5 traffic complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.29, severity: high)
700% spike coincides with multiple active ULURP rezonings (Northern Boulevard, 24th Avenue, Horace Harding Expressway)
541 DOB permits filed in last 90 days suggest ongoing construction activity that may be impacting traffic flow
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations against active construction sites and ULURP projects to identify which development is causing bottlenecks
Interview residents on Northern Boulevard and 24th Avenue about commute delays and whether construction notifications were adequate

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Reports
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints surged to 5 THIS WEEK—a 567% increase from the 0.8 weekly baseline—potentially signaling aggressive site clearing or construction-related tree removal tied to the district's active rezoning pipeline.
evidence: 5 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.13, severity: high)
567% spike temporally linked to 5 active ULURP applications and 68 new building permits filed in 90 days
Illegal tree damage typically a marker of uncontrolled demolition or site prep without proper environmental review
reporting_angles: Cross-reference complaint addresses with DOB permit and ULURP sites to determine if developers are removing trees without approval
Obtain 311 complaint detail to assess whether damage is incidental or systematic, and whether violations have been issued

themes_detail.label: Homeless Assistance Requests Surge
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance calls jumped to 4 THIS WEEK—a 700% spike from the 0.5 weekly baseline—suggesting either an emerging encampment or increased vulnerability among unhoused residents in Bayside/Douglaston neighborhoods.
evidence: 4 homeless person assistance complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.04, severity: high)
700% spike is sudden and sustained; warrants investigation into cause (economic displacement, shelter capacity, weather-driven migration)
Community board budget repeatedly requests senior center programs (01 request), suggesting aging population; may be intersecting vulnerability
reporting_angles: Identify specific locations of 311 complaints to assess whether there is a concentration (e.g., parks, transit hubs, commercial districts)
Interview local service providers, precinct commanders, and community leaders about whether homelessness is perceived as a new or worsening trend
